faq: Can any seller build a brand page?
Amazon Stores need a registered brand, while eBay Stores and Etsy shops have their own plans. We check what your account allows first. We cannot get around marketplace eligibility rules.
Do you use my own images?

Yes, please send high resolution brand and product photos. Premium includes designed banners using your images and style. We do not use pictures from other sellers or stock images that misrepresent your products.
Can I edit the page afterwards?
Yes. The pages use the marketplace's builder, which you can open in your own account. Premium includes style notes so new sections look like they belong. Larger edits can be quoted separately.
Does a brand page improve my ranking?
Not directly. It gives shoppers a place to browse, helps your ads land somewhere useful and builds trust. We build it to make the products easy to find, and we do not promise any rise in sales.

desc:
An Amazon brand store and storefront design gives shoppers a branded home inside the marketplace, away from competitor ads. Ecom Swift LLC plans, writes and builds your brand page in the marketplace's own page builder, ready for your approval.

## What is an Amazon brand store?

An Amazon brand store is a free multi-page storefront that registered brand owners build inside the marketplace. It has its own web address within Amazon and can include a home page, category pages and product grids. Other marketplaces offer similar branded shop areas, with different tools and limits.

The page is the one place where you decide the layout, the images and the order products appear. Search results and product pages are shared with every competitor. A brand page is not.

## Why a branded page deserves real effort

Shoppers who click your brand name want to see more than a list. If they land on a flat grid with no story, no grouping and no clear next step, they leave for a competitor's page. A plain page also misses the chance to send visitors to related products.

Planning matters before any building starts. Which products come first, how they are grouped and which images carry the brand all affect how the page reads on a phone, where much of the browsing happens.

## How a brand page supports sales

A good storefront works by reducing effort. Shoppers who arrive from your ads, social posts or packaging inserts can see the full range in one place and move straight to the product they want. Grouping by need, such as gifts, travel or kitchen, helps people who do not yet know the exact item.

Cross-links keep a visitor inside your range after viewing one product. We make no claim about ranking, because the marketplace does not publish how brand pages affect search. The page improves clarity and brand recall, and what it changes in your sales depends on your products and traffic.

## What a strong brand page includes

- A header image and logo that match your packaging and your other channels.
- A short brand story that says who you are and what makes the range useful.
- Featured product tiles chosen for margin, popularity and availability.
- Category pages grouped around how shoppers actually search.
- Bestseller and new arrival sections that you can refresh later.
- Lifestyle photos that show the product in use, sized to the page builder's tiles.
- A video tile, where you supply approved footage.
- Navigation that works on a phone as well as a desktop screen.
- Clean text with no claims the marketplace would reject.

## How we build it

We begin with a short planning session: your best sellers, the order of the page and the images you have. Then we write the brand copy and build the store in your own account using the tiles the marketplace allows. You review a preview, request changes and approve it before it is published.

The Basic package builds a single page with your top products. Standard adds category pages, a bestseller section and a navigation menu. Premium covers a larger storefront with custom banner images, a campaign page, cross-links and a style note so later updates match.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Lead with your best-selling and best-reviewed products.
- Use sharp images at the sizes the builder asks for.
- Keep brand copy short and specific to what you sell.
- Check the page on a phone before publishing.
- Update seasonal sections as stock and offers change.

**Avoid:**
- Using images that carry another brand's logo or text the marketplace forbids.
- Filling the page with every product regardless of relevance.
- Writing pricing or shipping claims that can go out of date.
- Letting out-of-stock items sit in prominent tiles.
- Copying a competitor's layout and wording.

## Who it is for

A brand owner with a registered brand and a growing range, who wants the storefront to look as considered as the packaging. A seller driving outside traffic from ads or social media, who needs a landing place inside the marketplace. A business preparing for a seasonal push, which needs a campaign page ready before the date.

## What we need from you

Send your logo, brand colors, product images and a list of the products to feature. You must be the registered brand owner on the marketplace to build a store. We never ask for passwords. We work through access you grant in the seller account, and you stay in control of publishing.
